subject: Readiness checkpoint — docs exception & staged onboarding for Atlas rollout
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Hudson <sara.hudson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Readiness checkpoint — docs exception & staged onboarding for Atlas rollout

Team / Sara —

Quick status and a proposal for the atlas (private VPC) customer launch planned for 2028-09-20. We have a content gap that could block a full launch, and I want to propose a controlled exception + staged onboarding to keep the go-live date while mitigating support risk.

Summary of gaps (from Docs & CS):
- Quickstart tutorial (walkthrough + example config) — draft only (attached v0.9).
- Troubleshooting KB for common errors (auth / certs / region routing) — stubbed sections.
- Customer-facing CS playbook (onboarding checklist + escalation steps) — initial outline.

Proposed compromise:
1) Proceed with a canary (US-East) for 2 weeks starting 2028-09-20 with a 50-customer cap and manual gating.
2) Require the following before canary: onboarding-runbook PDF (finalized), one live onboarding session with ACME, and a 24/7 triage rota for the first 48h of canary.
3) Engineering to expose a feature-flag to disable auto-scaling for the canary tenants and an immediate rollback toggle.

Asks:
- Marissa: confirm whether we can operate the canary process (SLAs, monitoring, support rota).
- Vivek / Rishi: confirm engineering work for the flag + rollback and estimate (hours).
- Laura: confirm CS capacity for 48h intensive support and if the attached playbook is sufficient to start training.
- Sara (ACME): would a staged onboarding + a runbook and a 60-minute kickoff session satisfy your go/no-go?

Attachments: onboarding-guide-v0.9.docx (docx, 245KB), cs-playbook-stub.md (md, 12KB), canary-rollout-matrix.xlsx (xls, 42KB)

Thanks — Camila
Camila Reyes
Program Manager, Product Launches
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Readiness checkpoint — docs exception & staged onboarding for Atlas rollout

Camila —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Short answers up front: I support a canary but with stricter controls. A few operational notes:

- Support risk: without a complete Troubleshooting KB we will run a lot of reactive tickets. We can cover that with a triage rota but need a published internal FAQ (even a short one) before 09/20.
- SLAs: We should mark canary tenants as "best-effort" in the console and set customer expectations in the kickoff. Legal asked to avoid promising uptime SLOs during canary.
- Monitoring: Ops needs two additional dashboards (error-rate by tenant, onboarding failure rate). I can spin these up by EOD 09/17 if I have the final list of signals.

Action items for my team:
- Publish internal FAQ (short) by 09/18.
- Run the canary runbook and own manual gating decisions.
- Coordinate with CS for the 48h rota.

One more ask — limit canary to 1 region (you suggested US-East) and tag all canary requests so we can filter logs without touching prod config.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Release Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Sara Hudson <sara.hudson@acmehealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 12:20:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Readiness checkpoint — docs exception & staged onboarding for Atlas rollout

Hi Camila / team —

ACME Health is happy to do a staged onboarding if it helps keep us on the 09/20 timeline. We require:
- A written runbook for our engineers (PDF) that includes certificate steps and example curl requests.
- A single 60-minute kickoff with your platform engineers (we can do 09/19 morning).
- A clear rollback path so we can be un-provisioned quickly if something breaks (our security team wants this).

If you can provide the runbook and confirm a kickoff, we will accept the canary approach. We prefer the canary be limited to non-production patient flows initially (demo/test dataset) — please confirm.

Thanks,
Sara Hudson
Director of Infrastructure, ACME Health
sara.hudson@acmehealth.com
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Sara Hudson <sara.hudson@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 13:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Readiness checkpoint — docs exception & staged onboarding for Atlas rollout

Folks —

Thanks for the quick replies — summary and next steps below. (Quoted earlier for context.)

Decision: Proceed with a limited canary starting 2028-09-20, US-East only, capped at 50 canary customers (ACME one of them) using demo/test dataset, with manual gating.

Immediate deliverables (owners & dates):
- Camila: Final runbook PDF for ACME and internal FAQ published by 09/18 (I will finish the runbook and share a drive link by EOD today).
- Marissa: Dashboards and gating process by 09/17; will operate manual gating and own the canary window.
- Vivek / Rishi: Feature-flag (disable auto-scale) + manual rollback toggle; estimate requested (ETA 09/16).
- Laura: CS triage rota for first 48h confirmed by 09/18; confirm training slot for ACME on 09/19.

Risks noted: incomplete KB and support pressure. We'll mitigate with the rota and a firm communication plan to ACME that this is a staged test on demo data.

Camila

Date: Sat, 15 Sep 2028 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Readiness checkpoint — docs exception & staged onboarding for Atlas rollout

Camila / team —

We can deliver the engineering gating items. Quick summary: 
- Feature-flag to disable autoscaling for canary tenants: ~6 dev hours + 4 QA hours, target 2028-09-16 EOD.
- Manual rollback/unprovision script (safe path to revoke tenant in 5 minutes): ~8 dev hours + 6 ops hours, target 2028-09-16 EOD.
- We'll add a tenant tag for easy filtering and include it in the telemetry pipeline.

Constraints / notes:
- The rollback script will deactivate provisioning and purge a temporary KV-cache; database migrations are not part of the canary. If we see any schema-related issues, we'll pause and roll back fully.
- We need a single owner for release-time decisions; please confirm if Marissa should be the gating owner (recommended).

If Marissa is gating owner and CS confirms rota, engineering greenlights the canary.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Platform Engineering
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
